```text
# #2267: Patch: hand hints, a tiny icon row on the viewer's own hand cards
Opened by @MaxGoetzmann.

## What it does

Adds a small, shared system for **hand hints**: tiny icons drawn on the viewer's own hand cards that say something about the card at a glance. This issue only builds the system and ships no hint. Two follow-ups each add a hint on top of it (a Tribute count and a Tradable mark), and later hints should reuse it too.

Hand cards are small, and a hand can hold a lot of them in an overlapping fan (`game/Hand.tsx`, `.hand-cards` with `--n`, board.css), so **the main requirement is that the hints stay out of the way**:

- **Where:** one compact row in a single corner of the face, inset from the edge, that never covers the cost, the name, the attack/health or the art's focal area. Pick the corner that stays visible when cards overlap in the fan (the part of a card the next card does not cover), and keep it there on the phone layout too (`board.css`'s narrow-screen `.hand-you .card-hand` rules).
- **Size:** each hint is a small pip, sized in `em` against the hand card so it scales with the card (around a tenth of the card's width; it must still read at the smallest hand-card size). It holds an icon and, where its hint has one, a single short number. A card with no hints draws nothing at all: no empty row, no box.
- **Look:** quiet. Low contrast, a thin outline or a soft backing so it reads over any art, no glow and no motion. A "dimmed" state (lower opacity, desaturated) that a hint can turn on. It follows the light/dark theme and the card's cosmetics do not change it.
- **Behaviour:** `pointer-events: none`, so every click, tap, lift and drag still reaches the card exactly as now (`Hand.tsx`'s capture-phase lift, `game/drag/DragLayer.tsx`). Each pip has text for screen readers (visually hidden, or `aria-label`) through `t()` (`i18n/i18n.ts`); the hover preview and inspect sheet stay as they are and are not the place for hints.
- **Who sees them:** only the viewer's own hand cards (`Hand.tsx`, the `yours` branch). The opponent's backs never get one (SPEC §10.8; they have nothing to read anyway), and neither do the revealed cards at game end (R434), the board, the deck builder or the collection.
- **The data:** a hint is computed only from what the view already gives the client (the `CardView`, the `PlayerView`), never from rules logic (CLAUDE.md rule 7). Hints are declared in one place, one module (for example `game/handHints.ts`, a list of `{ id, icon, applies(card, view) → null | { n?: number, dimmed?: boolean, label: string } }`), and a component (for example `game/HandHints.tsx`) draws whatever the list returns, in the list's order. Adding a hint is one entry in the list plus its icon; nothing else changes.
- **Icons:** in the same style as the other small SVG icons in `cards/icons.tsx`.

Read `apps/web/README.md` before you start (Game.tsx's layers each have one owning module; this is a new one, owned by hand rendering, not by `cards/CardFace.tsx`).

## Acceptance

- A vitest unit test for the hint module: a hint that returns null draws nothing; a card with no hints renders no hint row element at all; a card with two hints renders two pips in the list's order; `n` is printed when given; `dimmed: true` sets the dimmed state (for example `data-dimmed="true"`).
- A vitest test on `Hand.tsx`: the hint row appears on the viewer's own hand cards only, never on the opponent's backs or on revealed hand cards (R434).
- A test that the pips take no pointer event (the hint row's computed style or class), and that a click on a hint row still lifts and selects the card.
- Each pip has an accessible label through `t()`.
- Ships with a test-only hint (in the test file, not in the shipped list): the shipped list starts empty, so this issue changes nothing a player sees.
- `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck`, `pnpm --dir apps/web test` and `pnpm exec eslint apps/web e2e` pass.

## Blocked by, part of

Blocks the Tribute and Tradable hand hints (linked from those issues).
```
